chapter_theme: The Videha king musters and reviews a vast army of elephants, horses, chariots and foot, marches under good omens into the Emangatha country and camps near the usurper's city, while ill omens fill Kattiyangaran's palace; the usurper, unaware, exchanges gifts with the king who means to kill him by feigned friendship.

cast.role: king of the Videhas, Civakan's maternal uncle, who feigns alliance with the usurper (விதையத்தார் வென்றி வேந்தன் 2153, விதையத் தார்கோன் 2176; not named in these verses)
the one who shows the army to the king in 2167, perhaps its commander
the usurping minister now ruling Civakan's father's city
the pleasure women of the usurper's palace
the world the narrator addresses in 2176

2152.reading: The day after the strapped, bull-hide drum had proclaimed the muster, conches, muzhavus and drums roared like a wind-beaten sea, and an army fierce as angry Death massed until the rich earth sagged, the gleam of its white swords spreading like the milk ocean.
2152.nuance: பின்னாள் ties the muster to the drum of 2150 and 2151, which announced the king's false alliance with the usurper.
2152.event: The day after the proclamation, the Videha king's army musters to the noise of conch and drum.

2153.reading: Like the bright sun that rises on the brow of the eastern mountain scattering the thick dark with saffron rays, the victorious king of the Videhas appears under a white umbrella on top of his lime-white mansion and looks over his fine army.
2153.event: The Videha king reviews his army from the roof of his palace.

2154.reading: The war elephants are described: trunks like palm trunks, killing with all five of their weapons, white as sea conch and fresh milk, roaring back at the great tiger's roar, strong enough to tear a mountain, their seven limbs well formed and touching the firm ground, and unmatched in fire-spitting fury.
2154.nuance: ஏழுறுப்புந் திண்ணிலந் தோய்வ names the mark of a fine elephant, seven parts reaching the ground; which five parts kill (ஐந்தினுங் கொல்வ) the verse does not list.

2155.reading: The elephants hung with bells on both flanks rage and fight their own shadows when they catch its scent, dark as loosening rain clouds and running with must, and the poet gives their numbers by the thousand: herds that pour must while kites cry over them, young ones, and as many tuskers.
2155.nuance: The counts are built from compounds (அறுபதிற்றறுபது, இராயிரம், இராயிரத்தைஞ்ஞூறு) whose grouping is not certain, so the total cannot be fixed.

2156.reading: The elephant riders are masters of lance, sword and bow who would fight Death itself, men who could make their mounts fly at a word, whose whole bodies iron had bitten in earlier battles, who ride elephants unafraid of blazing fire, a crore of them living by this work.
2156.nuance: கோடியே விருத்தியா வுடையார் makes them a standing force living by war, not levies.

2157.reading: The horses are counted: twice six thousand that bathe in saffron water in their stalls, sixty thousand with white plumes and gold trappings, armoured in silver against arrows, that would not stay on the ground if let go, and a host past telling hung with green-rayed chowries.
2157.nuance: ஆறாயிரத் திரட்டி may be twice six thousand or a doubled troop of six thousand.

2158.reading: The horsemen, skilled to the end in gleaming lance, sword, bows curved like a snake shedding its skin and other arms, flawless men of high birth who have seen a thousand battlefields and wear moon-white ornaments, mount their harnessed war horses.
2158.event: The cavalry mount their harnessed horses.

2159.reading: Some of the horses are lotus-coloured and fierce, with flawless hooves, from Malava; others, perfect in form, coloured like the fruit of a full-branched jambu and dancing to the drum, come from the banks of the cool Sindhu.
2159.nuance: Whether the verse names one breed or two (Malava and the Sindhu) depends on how its four lines are grouped.

2160.reading: Horses born in lands called Parasa, Suravam and Pallava, heroic in strength and coloured like strong ripe toddy, would think it a great disgrace to walk on the earth and, ashamed, leap into the sky so that the long rain clouds shake.
2160.nuance: பார சூரவம் பல்லவம் is a list of foreign horse countries whose division into names is not secure.

2161.reading: Horses beautiful as the peacock's neck, from the Maratta country, with bodies coloured like young parrots and hooves like sea coral, came down from ships that sail the battling sea.

2162.reading: Chariots of fine make, harnessed to such full-maned horses, shine with gold, silver and gems as if they had taken the white moon for their home, and their number is twenty thousand and six hundred.
2162.nuance: இயறோ is read as இயல் தேர், and the count as twenty thousand ending in six hundred; வெண் மதியத் தன்னை யூர்கொண்ட is hard to construe.

2163.reading: The chariot warriors, with swords that burn like the sun at noon over the sea and practised in thrown weapons beyond the sword, feed their enemies to Death every day.

2164.reading: The foot soldiers are like tigers striking with their teeth, trained in bow, sword and spear alike, hearers of much instruction, picked out from many, and able with sharp weapons to cut down the fury of rutting elephants.
2164.nuance: துயிற்றியபல் கேள்வியினர் is obscure; it may mean men whose much learning has settled, or something else.

2165.reading: They are like Death with its train of fierce diseases, able to fill the roaring sea and dig up mountains, renowned in manly work, four lakhs in number, who have besides won a place of special trust.
2165.nuance: மேலும் நுமரால் addresses someone as 'your people'; the addressee is not clear from the verse.

2166.reading: Lion-skin shields, swords, spears and bows spread out together and flashed like lightning, moon and sun among clouds, so that even Death of the fierce eye took to a fortress.
2166.nuance: கூற்றுமரண் சேர is read as Death itself seeking shelter in fear; it could instead say the army spread to reach the enemy's fort.
2166.event: The armed host spreads out its shields and weapons.

2167.reading: The one who wore the ring of fresh gold showed the army to the king of kings, the bright-anklet king mounted his Airavata of an elephant till it grew hot, and the host cheered 'may he win'.
2167.nuance: Who ஆழி தொட்டான் is, the commander or another, the verse does not say; அயிராவணம் names the elephant after Indra's.
2167.event: The army is presented to the king, who mounts his elephant amid cries of victory.

2168.reading: Small white conches sounded, strong drums roared like the sea and the rain cloud, birds and other signs favoured the road, and the king's right eye throbbed in accord.
2168.nuance: The right eye's throb is a good sign here for a man; 2173 gives the same throb to the usurper's women as an ill one.
2168.event: Good omens attend the king's setting out.

2169.reading: With the ringing bells of the great elephants, the clatter of the five-gaited horses, the shout and the flashing swords like lightning, the army moved like a great sea.

2170.reading: Under white umbrellas like the evening moon and the cool shade of peacock-feather parasols, with the three musts of the elephants pouring down like a grove's rain, the land the army crossed turned from desert into fertile field.
2170.nuance: The hyperbole makes the army a giver of water: பாலை போய் மருதம் பயந்திட்டது turns a march into a change of tinai.

2171.reading: Peacocks of the commons rose screaming, herds of deer with their fawns scattered, and fearing the victorious spear-army it looked as if the hills and their forests were moving away.

2172.reading: Passing many hills and forests whose falling streams sounded like drums, after reaching the Emangatha country, the king took a golden walled place whose top touched the moonlight as the guard of his camp and as his palace.
2172.nuance: கடிமண் காவல் and கோயிலாகக் கருதினான் are read as camp and palace; the doubled கருதினான் is unusual.
2172.event: The army reaches the Emangatha country and the king makes camp in a walled enclosure.

2173.reading: In the usurper's palace the pleasure women's right eyes throbbed and they saw evil dreams, the king's body lost its lustre, owls hooted by day in the palace with dreadful cries, the victory drum lost its voice, blood rained from the sky, and earth and sky shook.
2173.nuance: Each sign reverses one of 2168's: the throbbing right eye, the drum that now falls silent, the birds; the verse states the portents and does not say what they portend.

2174.reading: Not knowing that Death had come and camped outside, the ruler of the rich land rejoiced that he sat there in splendour and with care sent two hundred victorious elephants, a hundred wind-swift chariots and a thousand fierce horses, decked in red-gold armour.
2174.nuance: கூற்றம் is the camped army itself; the narrator's word makes the guest Death before the host knows it.
2174.event: Kattiyangaran sends elephants, chariots and horses as gifts to the Videha king, whose army is camped near his city.

2175.reading: The king there sent back, decked in gold, one rutting elephant called Vari Manalan, the chariot Vijayam with its lightning banner and the horse Pavana Vegam, and the usurper, not seeing what was coming, was delighted and praised him for returning twice the elephants he had sent.
2175.nuance: நிகழ்வது ஓரான் gives the narrator's view; the usurper reads three named mounts as more than his hundreds, a measure of worth he does not see is bait.
2175.event: The Videha king returns named gifts, and Kattiyangaran, deceived, praises his generosity.

2176.reading: The narrator announces that he will now tell the world how the Videha king, making himself one with Kattiyangaran, plotted by deceit to seize and devour his life with the sharp sword called love.
2176.nuance: அன்பெனு மயில்கொள் வாள் names the false friendship as the weapon, and வஞ்சம் is the narrator's own word for the hero's side's plan.

links.note: In 2149 the Videha king tells his counsellors that as the usurper meant to kill him by deceit, they will take his life by deceit, and bids them keep it secret; 2176 has the narrator announce that very plan, with love as its sword.
links.teaches: The secret the king swore his counsellors to keep is opened to the audience but not to the victim, so the listener watches the gifts of 2174 and 2175 knowing what the usurper cannot, and the narrator names the plan deceit without blaming it.

links.note: In 2148 the king laughs at the letter that the wretch is calling Death with his own hand; in 2174 the usurper does not know that Death has come and camped outside.
links.teaches: The king's jest becomes the narrator's description: the Death the usurper summoned by letter now sits at his gate, and the gifts he sends out are his welcome to it.

links.note: The king's right eye throbs as a good sign and his drums roar as he sets out; in the usurper's palace the women's right eyes throb, owls cry by day and the victory drum falls silent.
links.teaches: The poet gives the two camps the same signs with opposite values, the throbbing right eye good for the marching king and bad for the palace women, the drum loud in one and dumb in the other, so the omen code is read by sex and by side.

links.note: Kural 830 counsels that when a foe must be treated as a friend, one should befriend with the face and drop friendship within; the Videha king makes himself one with the usurper so as to kill him by the sword of love.
links.teaches: The couplet's face-friendship is a defensive mask with an exit, while the epic turns it into the method of a killing and calls it வஞ்சம் even on the hero's side, so the pair shows how far the Kural's permission can be stretched once the foe is a usurper.

gains.a: the epic's ruse gains a rule of statecraft that makes a just king's deceit look like prudence rather than treachery
gains.b: the couplet gains a case where the outward friendship is not a passing shelter but the weapon itself, which its own wording does not reach

links.note: Kural 882 bids one fear the bond with enemies who are like kin more than enemies like swords; the usurper delights in the kinsman-like gifts of the king who means to kill him.
links.teaches: The couplet's warning is spoken to the potential victim, and the epic shows that victim praising the gift that should have frightened him, while placing the kin-like enemy on the side the story favours.

gains.a: the scene gains a name for the usurper's error: he guarded against the sword but not against the friend
gains.b: the couplet gains a plot in which its danger is visible to everyone but the one it warns, and in which the false friend is not the villain

links.note: Purananuru 20 says the Chera's guard is not shaken by omen birds coming or going; in the usurper's palace owls cry by day, blood rains and earth and sky shake.
links.teaches: Read together the two make portents a measure of rule: the praised king's realm is not shaken whatever the birds do, while the usurper's palace is shaken by every sign, though the epic does not itself say his usurpation is the cause.

gains.a: the epic's portents gain a puram standard by which a secure realm is one omens cannot move, which marks the usurper's as already lost
gains.b: the poem's claim gains its counter-case, a palace where the omens do strike, which shows what the praise of immunity is set against

new_concepts.gloss: an omen or sign read as foretelling what will come
new_concepts.label_source: label from 1129; here the verse's own word நிமித்தமு (2168, line 3)

source_issues: 2152-2158 and 2173-2176 were printed in eight half-lines and joined into four (FLAG repaired); the joins read correctly.
2155 and 2157: the army's counts are compounds whose grouping is not certain (அறுபதிற்றறுபது, இராயிரத்தைஞ்ஞூறு, ஆறாயிரத் திரட்டி).
2160 line 1 பார சூரவம் பல்லவம்: the division of the horse-country names is doubtful.
2162 line 1 இயறோ and lines 2-3 வெண் மதியத் தன்னை யூர்கொண்ட are hard to construe; 2163 line 1 நொச்சி மாமலர் நிறத்தன has no clear subject.
2172 line 2 has a doubtful division (இசையோவாவேமாங் கதநாட்டெய்தியபி); the place name ஏமாங்கதம் is read from it.
